description:
Issue summary: After TLS client-certificate rotation on HelixMed on-prem cluster, scheduled batch inference workers started receiving 403s when attempting to call the Redwood private API. Impact: All scheduled batch jobs that run under the HelixMed service account 'svc-batch-infer' have failed since 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC. Approx 12 jobs failed in the first hour, causing delayed processing of overnight datasets.

Observed behavior: Ingress-proxy is accepting TLS client certs but the principal resolved by our auth pipeline is a user principal (email-based) instead of the intended service principal (uri-based spn:svc-batch-infer). RBAC lookups fail (no service account binding for the resolved user), resulting in 403 responses from the authz layer.

Environment: private on-prem deployment behind customer-managed edge (HAProxy -> ingress-proxy v1.11.3 -> private-control-plane). Problem started immediately after cert rotation performed by customer automation (ACME-like tooling) which now issues certs containing both an email SAN and a URI SAN for compatibility.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use the HelixMed client certificate bundle with subjectAltName ordering: email:first, URI:second (sample cert attached in support portal).
2) Initiate a scheduled batch job that uses the node-level service account mTLS authentication.
3) Observe the auth pipeline logs on ingress-proxy and the private-control-plane audit logs.
4) Confirm resulting 403s from authz with message: "principal not bound to any service account".

Logs / evidence:
- ingress-proxy auth log (2026-03-10T02:16:03Z): "Parsed principal: user:helix.j.smith@example.com (from SAN email)"
- authz evaluation (2026-03-10T02:16:03Z): "lookup service account for principal 'spn:svc-batch-infer' -> not found"
- control-plane audit (2026-03-10T02:16:03Z): "request denied: rolebinding not found for principal user:helix.j.smith@example.com"
- Customer-provided cert (PEM) shows SAN sequence: email:helix.j.smith@example.com, URI:spn:svc-batch-infer

Initial hypothesis: A change in the TLS parsing semantics in the ingress-proxy's underlying TLS library (Go TLS update in v1.11.3 -> uses go1.21 runtime) altered which SAN extension is chosen as the canonical principal when multiple SAN types are present. Earlier behavior favored URI SAN for principal selection; new behavior favors the first SAN in certificate order (email). This causes our principal-mapper to map to user principals when certs include an email SAN before the URI SAN.

Business impact: P1 - production data processing delays for customer HelixMed. This is customer-impacting for their private deployment and may affect other on-prem customers who rotated certs with both SAN types.

Attachments: PEM of rotated client cert (redacted), ingress-proxy logs excerpt, control-plane audit excerpt, customer automation config snippet.
comments: 2026-03-10 04:12 - Support (Maya): Received initial report from HelixMed SOC - overnight batch failures after cert rotation. Escalated to infra oncall.
2026-03-10 05:05 - Oncall (Rohit): Reproduced locally with provided cert. Confirmed principal parsed as email-based user. Opening INT-4402 to track internal code-level investigation.

2026-03-10 08:30 - SRE (Lena Ortiz): Ingress-proxy TLS parsing was upgraded in 1.11.3. Reproduced behavior by swapping SAN ordering; observed mapping change. Creating PR to add explicit SAN selection logic to prefer URI with spn: prefix for service principals.

2026-03-11 10:17 - Customer (HelixMed - Ops): Workaround applied by regenerating certs without the email SAN. Batch jobs cleared. Customer requests timeline for permanent fix and asks whether other customers are impacted.

2026-03-12 11:45 - Eng (Rohit): Rolling patch prepared to normalize principal selection. Patch will prefer URI SAN with 'spn:' prefix when present, otherwise fallback to email SAN. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/1427
2026-03-12 16:00 - Support (Maya): Notified HelixMed of the workaround and expected patch window. Scheduled a post-deploy verification with the customer for 2026-03-14.
investigation_notes: Reproduced with OpenSSL s_client and sample certs; swapping SAN order reproduces the principal selection change.
Ingress-proxy uses x509 package's 'Certificate.Subject' canonicalization path which relies on first-match SAN selection in current code path.

Service account principal format used by customers is 'spn:<name>' encoded in URI SAN in certs. Our principal-mapper currently checks SAN types in fixed order: DNS -> Email -> URI, which is fragile when certs include multiple SAN types.
SRE confirmed only on-prem customers who included email SANs in client certs are likely impacted; hosted customers use bearer tokens.
Edge case: some corporate CAs add an email SAN by default; recommend communicating to customers this certificate compatibility note until release.
Add telemetry to auth pipeline to log SAN kind chosen for principal resolution (opt-out by default).
resolution: Workaround: HelixMed regenerated client certs omitting the email SAN (kept URI SAN 'spn:svc-batch-infer') which restored service. Permanent fix: ingress-proxy patch will explicitly prefer URI SANs that start with 'spn:' when mapping to service principals; otherwise fall back to existing selection order. Patch PR created and tests added for SAN ordering. Deploy plan: canary in staging 2026-03-14, prod roll on 2026-03-15 during maintenance window. Post-deploy verification scheduled with HelixMed. Communicate advisory to on-prem customers recommending certs include spn: URI SAN or avoid adding email SANs.
postmortem_followup: Add unit tests for SAN selection to prevent regression.
Run a query across on-prem fleets to detect certs that include both email and URI SANs and notify impacted customers.
Document recommended cert profile for service accounts in Private Deployments admin guide.
Add telemetry to auth pipeline to log SAN kind chosen for principal resolution (opt-out by default).
